page: Amazon Web Services g7e.48xlarge is a graphics-intensive, memory-optimized, and storage-heavy server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs powered by 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 2.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2048.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, the instance is equipped with eight NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 768 GB of VRAM. Storage is supported by 15200 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 400 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the g7e.48xlarge in the top tier for multiple performance categories. The multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, and the memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks rank in the top 10% of tested systems. The instance also demonstrates top-tier capabilities in cryptographic and database operations, with Redis SET operations reaching 201.69 million operations per second. For artificial intelligence workloads, the system achieves top-tier LLM inference speeds, processing prompts at 1269.37 tokens per second and generating text at 28.08 tokens per second on large 70B models.

Given its dense integration of eight professional-grade GPUs, massive DDR5 memory capacity, and extensive local NVMe storage, the g7e.48xlarge represents a highly consolidated hardware profile. This resource density offers qualitative cost efficiency by reducing the need to distribute complex workloads across multiple smaller nodes, thereby minimizing inter-node network latency and cluster management overhead. The instance is suited for demanding workloads such as large-scale LLM inference, multi-threaded data decompression, ray tracing, real-time image processing, and high-throughput database operations.
